passages.locator: did not begin with a formulated moral message
passages.excerpt_preview: n interviews with Andrew Robinson, Ray said he did not begin with a formulated moral message and preferred critics to draw conclusions from the films.
He recalled gaining confidence in directing through Pather Panchali.
The BFI notes that his young detective Feluda proved very popular and that Ray adapted two Feluda tales for cinema.

passages.locator: concentrated into shorter spans of time
passages.excerpt_preview: After the Apu Trilogy he preferred stories concentrated into shorter spans of time.
Discussing Goopy Gyne Bagha Byne, he described music drawing on Indian folk and classical traditions as well as Western orchestration.
Over his career he increasingly composed film scores and songs himself.
The interview separates Ray’s own account of method from critical claims about humanism or social meaning.
